1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. JSON: JavaScript Object Notation; MCP: Model Context Protocol

  • The core components: Rules, Skills, Commands, Agents and Agent Memory
  • Features: session management, slash commands, headless, streaming and auto mode
  • The CLAUDE.md hierarchy, repository initialization and settings.json

2Core Components

Running case

Tidewater Rolls Out Claude Code

  • Fifty engineers will use Claude Code on the claims platform
  • The lead wants shared standards, reusable workflows, specialist helpers, and safe automation

Component What it is Where it lives
CLAUDE.md Persistent instructions loaded at session start User ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, project CLAUDE.md or .claude/CLAUDE.md (shared), subdirectories
Rules Topic files, optionally scoped to paths with a glob .claude/rules/*.md
Skills On-demand procedures (SKILL.md with frontmatter) .claude/skills/<name>/ or ~/.claude/skills/
Commands /name shortcuts; custom commands are markdown files .claude/commands/ (shared) or ~/.claude/commands/ (personal); now merged into skills [Verify live]
Agents Subagents defined as markdown with frontmatter: own context, tools and optional memory .claude/agents/ or ~/.claude/agents/
Agent memory Knowledge a subagent keeps across sessions (user, project or local scope); also auto memory: notes Claude writes itself from your corrections Memory directories managed by Claude Code
settings.json Permissions, hooks, environment, plugins, model User, shared project, project local, managed

The CLAUDE.md hierarchy

  • User level: personal, not shared. Project level: shared through version control. Directory level: applies to work in that folder. Files are combined, not overridden; keep them short and specific.
  • /init analyzes the repository and creates a starting CLAUDE.md (build and test commands, conventions); review and edit it. /memory shows which memory files are loaded.
  • Repository initialization checklist: run /init, commit the project CLAUDE.md, add shared .claude/settings.json (permissions, hooks), add rules, skills and commands the team needs, and keep personal overrides in local files.
Exam tip

Team standards belong in the committed project CLAUDE.md and .claude/settings.json, not in a user file.

3Features

Feature What to know
Session management Sessions are saved: continue the latest (--continue), resume one by ID or name (--resume <name>, name with -n), fork to try another path (--fork-session); /clear starts fresh; /compact frees context
Slash commands Built-in (/init, /memory, /compact, /model, /permissions and more) and custom ones from markdown files
Headless mode claude -p "prompt" runs non-interactively and exits: for scripts and CI; add --output-format json (and --json-schema) for structured output
Streaming mode --output-format stream-json emits newline-delimited JSON events as they happen, for programs that show progress
Permission modes default (ask), acceptEdits, plan (read-only exploration), auto (a classifier reviews actions and allows or blocks them), dontAsk, bypassPermissions (isolated environments only)

  • Auto mode reduces prompts for autonomous runs while a classifier still reviews risky actions; bypassPermissions removes checks and belongs only in isolated environments.
  • In CI use -p, give context through CLAUDE.md, pre-approve needed tools with --allowedTools, and prefer limits such as --max-turns.

[Verify live] Flags and modes evolve (for example --bare skips auto-discovery of CLAUDE.md, hooks and MCP servers for scripted runs). As of 8 November 2026.

Exam tip

Shared project standards go in the committed project CLAUDE.md and .claude/settings.json; a script or CI job uses claude -p; a progress UI uses stream-json.

Exam tip

Headless (-p) is for scripts and CI; streaming JSON is for programs that show progress.

4Exam Q&A

S1A new teammate does not get the team's coding standards in Claude Code. Where were the standards most likely placed?

  • AIn the project's .claude/rules/
  • BIn one developer's user-level ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, not the committed file
  • CIn the repository's CLAUDE.md
  • DIn .claude/settings.json
Show the answer

Answer: B. User-level files are personal; project-level files travel with the repository.

S2What does /init do?

  • AAnalyzes the repository and creates a starting CLAUDE.md
  • BDeletes the session and all of the notes that it contains
  • CInstalls a plugin
  • DSwitches the model to the next larger tier for the rest of the session
Show the answer

Answer: A. /init drafts the project instructions for you to review and commit.

S3A pipeline must run Claude Code without waiting for input. Which option fits?

  • APlan mode
  • BA browser session
  • Cclaude -p "prompt"
  • DInteractive mode with a long timeout
Show the answer

Answer: C. The -p flag runs Claude Code non-interactively, prints the result and exits, which is what scripts need.

S4A program wants real-time progress events from a Claude Code run. Which output format fits?

  • ANo output
  • BA screenshot
  • CPlain text only
  • Dstream-json
Show the answer

Answer: D. Streaming JSON emits newline-delimited events as they happen, so a program can show progress.

S5Which TWO statements about Claude Code components are correct? Select TWO.

  • ASubagents are defined as markdown files with their own context and tools
  • BProject-level CLAUDE.md is shared through version control
  • CSlash commands cannot be customized
  • DSkills are always loaded in full at startup
  • EbypassPermissions is recommended for everyday laptops
Show the answer

Answer: A, B. Subagents and committed project instructions are core components; bypass mode is for isolated environments.
